text: When working with APIs, you interact with a server by sending HTTP requests to obtain or send data. Most APIs return information in JSON format, which is easy to read and use in programming. Before accessing data, you usually need authentication, often with a special key or token, to prove who you are. However, you must also respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain period. If you exceed these limits, the server may block you temporarily. Therefore, good error handling is essential—you need to check for problems like invalid keys or network issues and respond gracefully to keep your application reliable.
